newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-LEWIS ISN'T RETIRING, WILL RUN IN EUROPE, HIS MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-LEWIS ISN'T RETIRING, WILL RUN IN EUROPE, HIS MANAGER.

text.p: Nine-time Olympic champion Carl Lewis has no plans to retire this spring and is looking forward to a triumphant farewell tour of Europe, his manager said on Wednesday.
"Carl is not retiring," Joe Douglas said in a telephone interview from his Santa Monica, California, office. "He will be competing this year and will do a few meets next year."
But this summer most likely will be the 35-year-old American star's "last time in Europe," Douglas said.
"It definitely will be for outdoors," said Douglas, leaving the door open for possible indoor competitions for Lewis, who is under contract with Nike through 1998.

Douglas called "completely inaccurate" reports from Sydney, where Lewis ran this week, that quoted the 1996 Olympic long jump champion as saying his last competitive race would be in his hometown of Houston in June.
"He wants his last meet (of his career) to be in Houston, and when he said Houston at the press conference, someone assumed it would be this year," Douglas said. "But that is not correct."
Lewis is planning a full schedule of races in Europe and elsewhere this summer, although he will not compete in either the U.S. or world championships, Douglas said.

"We are talking to quite a few people," said Douglas, who runs the Santa Monica Track Club. "It will probably be some of the regular meets, some of the Golden Four, and there is a chance we would go over early and run in a few meets then.
